name: SCORPIO
question: Do mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg improve incontinence and urinary frequency over placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder for at least 3 months, at least 8 daily micturitions, and at least 3 urgency episodes in a 3-day baseline diary.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Khullar 2013 PubMed abstract, Design; Khullar 2013 post-hoc full text, Methods and Results, Table 1; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00689104, Participant Flow

verdictNote: Both mirabegron doses met both co-primary placebo comparisons at 12 weeks.
takeaway: In SCORPIO, mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg each reduced daily incontinence episodes and micturitions more than placebo over 12 weeks; tolterodine ER 4 mg was an active control without a prespecified head-to-head mirabegron comparison.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Khullar V, Amarenco G, Angulo JC, et al. "Efficacy and tolerability of mirabegron, a β(3)-adrenoceptor agonist, in patients with overactive bladder: results from a randomised European-Australian phase 3 trial." *Eur Urol.* 2013;63(2):283-295. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.10.016
reports.followUp: 12 weeks of double-blind treatment after a 2-week placebo run-in

results.measure: Adjusted mean change at final visit; mean difference in change, mirabegron 50 mg versus placebo
results.note: Difference calculated from the two adjusted mean changes reported in the abstract.

delivery.label: Study treatment
delivery.value: Once-daily oral placebo, mirabegron 50 mg, mirabegron 100 mg, or tolterodine ER 4 mg for 12 weeks after a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in; 1,978 randomized participants received study drug.
